parts.description: 15 min: attempt M0 and check it. 60 min: use Neha’s one-shot only for rate of change and related rates; pair it with NCERT §6.2, Examples 1, 2 and 4. Write the chain-rule setup before substituting values. If M0 exposes weak differentiation, use the first 20 minutes of this same learning allowance for Chapter 5 repair. 15 min: solve Exercise 6.1 Q1 and Q3 without viewing solutions.

65 min: solve Exercise 6.1 Q2, Q7, Q8, Q10, Q11, Q14, Q15 and Q16, in that order. Draw a diagram for the ladder/cone; state the changing variable and units. 20 min: check answers and redo the first two wrong setups. 5 min: record unfinished question numbers. Output: ten attempted NCERT questions with corrections, plus the M0 result.

15 min: attempt C0 and check it. 45 min: watch Bharat 03:25–12:50 and 27:00–57:40, pausing only for the redox/cell essentials; stop before Nernst. Read the Daniell-cell diagram alongside. Output: labelled cell, anode/cathode reactions, electron direction, salt-bridge role and E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode.

40 min: attempt NCERT in-text Q2.1–2.3 and end-exercise Q2.1–2.3. These are two different question lists. Use the standard-potential table for comparisons. 15 min: check using the cell explanation/table; fix electrode signs and the reducing-power order. 5 min: record one confusion or mark none. Output: six written answers and one correct cell diagram.

sessions.subject: Physics
sessions.title: Magnetic field laws and circular loop

parts.description: 15 min: attempt P0 and check it. 75 min: watch these Arvind segments in order: 01:05–23:07; 30:21–35:20; 58:30–1:29:55. Pause for the right-hand rule and the circular-loop axis derivation. Output: field directions plus the straight-wire, loop-centre and loop-axis formulas. The remaining field-law clips are after the break.

15 min: watch 1:52:35–1:59:29, 2:03:41–2:07:34 and 2:25:27–2:28:22. State Ampere’s law; learn the solenoid field pattern qualitatively. 60 min: solve end-exercise Q4.1–4.4, independently work Example 4.6, then reproduce the loop-axis derivation once with a labelled diagram. 15 min: check, correct and log. Skip thick-wire/solid-cylinder derivations and solenoid numerical Q4.8 in this board-focused stage.

sessions.subject: Chemistry
sessions.title: Nernst equation, Gibbs energy and equilibrium

parts.description: 40 min: watch Bharat 57:40–1:16:10, then read NCERT §2.3.1–2.3.2 and Examples 2.2–2.3. Write Q, n and the balanced reaction before each formula; cover E versus E°, ΔG° = −nFE° and log K = nE°/0.0591. 20 min: attempt in-text Q2.4 and Q2.5.

45 min: solve end-exercise Q2.4(i), Q2.4(ii), Q2.5(i) and Q2.5(iii). Complete all requested quantities in Q2.4; do not treat each as one short calculation. 15 min: compare with the supplied answer key and redo one mistaken Q/n/sign/log step. Output: six worked problems across the sitting, with calculations and units.

60 min: use the increasing/decreasing-functions portion of Neha’s one-shot with NCERT §6.3, Examples 10–12. Learn domain → derivative → critical points → sign chart → intervals. 30 min: solve Exercise 6.2 Q3, Q4 and Q5, including their requested intervals/subparts.

60 min: solve Exercise 6.2 Q6(a), Q6(c), Q7, Q8, Q14 and Q19. State the domain before logarithmic/rational work and show why a parameter meets the interval condition. 15 min: reattempt the earliest two wrong Monday questions; if none were wrong, do Exercise 6.1 Q12 and Q18. 15 min: check and correct today’s answers. Output: sign charts and one parameter-inequality solution, with no unexplained interval answers.

sessions.subject: Physics
sessions.title: Magnetic force, circular motion and conductor force

parts.description: 60 min: watch Arvind 2:32:07–2:58:30, 3:04:23–3:11:34 and 3:24:59–3:40:06. Write F=q(v×B), F=I(ℓ×B), r=mv/(|q|B) and T=2πm/(|q|B). Explain the force direction and why speed stays constant. Stop before the parallel-wire section.

45 min: independently work NCERT Examples 4.1 and 4.3, end-exercise Q4.5 and Q4.6, then P1’s four short questions. 15 min: check and redo the first wrong direction or orbit calculation. Output: two worked examples, two exercise questions and the short direction/motion drill. Use the constants printed in the specific question.

60 min: watch Bharat 1:16:10–1:46:25; then read NCERT §2.4, especially the dilution graphs and Kohlrausch’s law. Write a compact unit table for R, G, cell constant, κ and Λm; distinguish S m⁻¹ from S cm⁻¹. Work Example 2.4 after covering its solution. 30 min: solve end-exercise Q2.7, Q2.8 and Q2.9.

60 min: solve end-exercise Q2.10 (including the graph) and Q2.11, then in-text Q2.7–2.9. Use Λm/Λ°m for degree of dissociation where applicable. 15 min: reattempt the earliest wrong Nernst question; if none, solve end-exercise Q2.5(ii). 15 min: check units, graph interpretation and calculations. Output: one labelled conductivity graph, the dilution explanation and checked conductivity/Kohlrausch applications.

45 min: use Neha’s maxima/minima portion with NCERT §6.4 and §6.4.1, Examples 17, 19 and 27. Distinguish critical points, first/second derivative tests and endpoint comparison; note why f′=0 alone is insufficient. 15 min: solve Exercise 6.3 Q3(ii) and Q3(v).

45 min: solve Exercise 6.3 Q3(vi), Q5(i), Q5(ii), Q7 and Q11. Show the domain, classify extrema and compare endpoints when asked for absolute extrema. 15 min: check and correct. Output: examples of local extrema, a closed-interval comparison and a parameter found from stationarity.

90 min: watch Arvind 3:40:06–4:47:26 and 4:51:35–4:56:54. Take brief notes on force per unit length, attraction/repulsion, magnetic moment, torque, radial field, galvanometer principle and current/voltage sensitivity. Pause at the diagrams and derive the torque balance; avoid copying the entire lecture.

45 min: watch 5:05:15–5:23:43 and 5:27:21–5:39:44; derive shunt and series-resistance formulas and draw each connection. 35 min: solve end-exercise Q4.7, Q4.9 and Q4.10 plus Example 4.12. 10 min: check and log. Output: two correctly connected meter diagrams and four worked questions. Longer independent derivation practice is reserved for Sunday.

40 min: read NCERT §2.5, including both Faraday laws and Example 2.10. Use Bharat from 1:46:25 for the product-of-electrolysis explanation; stop at the end of that topic, with at most 15 minutes of video inside this allowance. Contrast active and inert electrodes. 20 min: solve end-exercise Q2.12 and Q2.13, all subparts.

45 min: solve end-exercise Q2.14, Q2.15, Q2.16 and Q2.18, all subparts. Prioritise Q2.15 and Q2.18 if time runs short. 15 min: check charge/electron stoichiometry and product predictions against NCERT §2.5 and the answer key. Output: m=MIt/nF used correctly, one series-cell calculation and products for active/inert-electrode cases.

sessions.subject: Chemistry
sessions.title: Batteries, fuel cells, corrosion and chapter check

parts.description: 45 min: read NCERT §2.6–2.8, PDF pp. 24–28. Make a compact table for dry cell, mercury cell, lead storage battery, nickel–cadmium cell and hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell: electrodes/reactants, reaction and rechargeable status where relevant. Draw rusting as local anodic/cathodic processes. 25 min: answer in-text Q2.13–2.15 from memory, then check the text. 20 min: repair the earliest unfinished/incorrect Chemistry core question; if none, solve exercise Q2.6.

45 min: attempt C-check closed-book. 30 min: mark with the supplied guide, write the reason for each lost mark and re-solve the first two wrong questions. 15 min: record score and remaining gaps. If the morning repair allowance did not clear a missing core concept, use this 45-minute test allowance to repair it and mark the check postponed; do not attempt an untaught topic for a score. Output: assessed Electrochemistry progress and exact carry-forward questions.

30 min: use Neha’s optimisation portion with NCERT Example 22 and Example 36. For every problem write variables → constraint → one-variable objective → domain → derivative → verification. 30 min: solve Exercise 6.3 Q13 and Q17. Draw the open-box diagram before differentiating.

45 min: solve Exercise 6.3 Q21 and Q24, then miscellaneous Q6 (minimum cost). These are three long problems, not a speed drill. 15 min: check the setup and extremum justification. If a long problem is unfinished, carry its number to Sunday’s repair allowance. Output: number-product, box, cylinder, cone and cost setups across the sitting.

60 min: write from memory the circular-loop axis field, straight-wire field using Ampere’s law, torque on a rectangular coil, galvanometer torque balance and both meter-conversion formulas, with diagrams where appropriate. Compare with NCERT and correct only missing steps. 30 min: solve exercise Q4.13 and repair the earliest wrong P0/Physics-core question. If no errors remain, reattempt Q4.10 without the key.

45 min: attempt P-check closed-book. 30 min: mark and re-solve the first two wrong questions. 15 min: update the topic checklist and carry-forward list. If a core topic remains untaught, replace the test with that repair and mark the test postponed. Output: a marked check and a list of the exact steps/topics still needing work.

sessions.subject: Maths
sessions.title: AOD chapter check and next-stage handover

parts.description: 45 min: attempt M-check closed-book. 15 min: mark it, keeping the first-attempt score separate from corrections. If Saturday left an untaught optimisation method, replace the test with that method and mark the check postponed.

25 min: correct the check’s lost-mark steps. 25 min: reattempt the earliest unfinished/incorrect Maths core question; if none, solve miscellaneous Q8 (window optimisation). 10 min: fill the three-subject handover: studied topics, independently correct types, pending question numbers and the first repair needed next week. Stop at 11:45 pm. Output: no vague “revise more” entries; every pending item has a topic or question number.
